question: At the same early dust time, does the finite candidate determine the areal radius for two masses uniformly in the admissible weights?
mass_choice: Extreme members of the three-mass P3 reference grid
time_choice: Earliest positive predeclared x on the common P3 grid with disjoint closed individual 5 percent reference-radius bands. No physical target values used in selecting x.
radius_rule: A radius is sqrt(A/(4 pi)) for the entire independently identified material surface at the given proper time. Test a closed triangulated cut with intrinsic lengths and externally controlled area error. Admit physical data only with independently prepared mass and a radius readout from the coupled histories.
ambiguity_test: Over the archived finite four-mark, nonnegative, one-edge support keep every earlier N13 marginal; assess all ten local end-weight vertices, without fixing the eight other coefficients to the old witness. Identify whether available data determine a coherent geometric readout. Compare two positive auxiliary radius assignments sharing the initial reference radius, slope and acceleration.
classification: Classical radii, independent synthetic geometry calibration, algebraic witnesses and physical CST radii are reported separately. A missing physical observable yields an undefined dynamical interval and HOLD. No physical ensemble or bounce test in this study.
